newsitem.title: INDIA: US Fed's McDonough for growth with price stability.
newsitem.headline: US Fed's McDonough for growth with price stability.

text.p: Price stability should be the prime determinant of monetary policy of central banks, the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said on Thursday.

"In my view, a key principle for monetary policy is that price stability is a means to an end -- to promote sustainable economic growth," Federal Reserve president William McDonough said in an address at the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
"Price stability is both important and desirable because a rising price level - inflation - even at moderate rates, imposes substantial economic costs on society," he said.

He detailed some of these costs - increased uncertainty about the outcome of business decisions and profitability, negative effects of interation of inflation with the tax system and distortions that create perverse incentives to engage in non-productive activities.

"Rapid moves toward price stability from high inflation, however, also have their costs," McDonough said. "The overdevelopment of a sector for no reason other than the inflation rate is precisely one possibility."
He said countries which witnessed an overexpansion of the financial sector also saw sharp contraction when inflation was finally brought down.
Such boom-bust cycles also strained a country's social fabric, pitting different groups in a society, he said.
A stable price and financial environment will enhance the capacity of monetary policy to fight occasions of cyclical weaknesses in the economy, McDonough said.
"Over the long run, price stability is the one sustainable contribution monetary policy can make to growth. This applies to all countries," he said.

Reserve Bank of India governor Chakravarty Rangarajan agreed with McDonough that price stability was crucial for growth but said threshold level where cost of inflation outweighed benefits differed from country to country.
For example, 2.0-2.5 percent was regarded as an ideal rate of inflation in many developed economies. "Some years ago, we though 4.0 percent (annual inflation rate) was tolerable."
"On the threshold level we will have to continue to experiment," he said.
